operation.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing charge usage. This posts to the same `/v2/api/entity/charge_usage` path as create; the record to update is identified by the **`id` in the request body**. If `id` is omitted a new record is created instead.

**Important — this is a partial overwrite, not a full merge.** The update always rewrites the foreign-key columns `credit_charge_id` and `credit_usage_id` and sets either of them **that you omit to null**. Because both are non-nullable, omitting one fails with a `400`. **Always resend `credit_charge_id` and `credit_usage_id` on every update.** `amount` is preserved if omitted.

On success the response is `{ "message": <localized text>, "id": <id> }`.

id.description: Id of the charge usage to update. Required — omitting it creates a new record instead.

credit_charge_id.description: Id of the credit charge. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is set to null (→ 400, non-nullable).

credit_usage_id.description: Id of the credit usage. Part of the core overwrite set — resend it or it is set to null (→ 400, non-nullable).

amount.description: Amount of credit consumed. Optional; preserved if omitted.

id.description: Id of the updated charge usage.

400.description: The update could not be saved — most commonly because a core foreign key (`credit_charge_id` or `credit_usage_id`) was omitted and nulled a non-nullable column.

e.description: Error detail. For a database-constraint failure: `{errorInfo, connectionName, readWriteType}`.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason (e.g. a core-set foreign key was omitted and nulled a non-nullable column).

401.description: The Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired.

403.description: The authenticated user lacks permission to manage credit usage.
